options: природа
природы
природе
природу
cases.translation: Nature does not ask your opinion.
cases.explain: Природа is the subject of спрашивается, so it stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Находит наконец до самого ___, до самого отомщения.
options: дело
дела
делу
делом
cases.translation: It finally gets down to the very deed, to the very act of revenge.
cases.explain: The preposition до (as far as/up to) governs the genitive case, hence дела.

cases.sentence: Столько других гадостей к одному ___ подвела столько неразрешенных вопросов.
options: вопрос
вопроса
вопросу
вопросом
cases.translation: It attached so many other nasty things to one single question, dragging in so many unresolved questions.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward/attached to) governs the dative case, hence вопросу.

cases.sentence: На вечную ___ о том, что даже в каменной-то стене как будто чем-то сам виноват.
options: тема
темы
теме
тему
cases.translation: On the eternal theme that even in the stone wall itself one is somehow to blame.
cases.explain: The preposition на expressing the topic ("on this theme") governs the accusative case, hence тему.

cases.sentence: Кстати, перед ___ такие господа, то есть непосредственные люди и деятели, искренне пасуют.
options: стена
стены
стене
стеной
cases.translation: Incidentally, before a wall such gentlemen, that is, immediate people and men of action, sincerely give up.
cases.explain: The preposition перед (in front of/before) governs the instrumental case, hence стеной.

options: стена
стены
стене
стеной
cases.translation: But more about the wall later.
cases.explain: The preposition о (about) governs the prepositional case, hence стене.

reading.ru: «Ведь у людей, умеющих за себя отомстить и вообще за себя постоять, как это, например, делается, ведь их, как обхватят положено чувство мести, так уж ничего больше во всем их существе на это время и не останется, кроме этого чувства».
reading.question: How does the narrator describe people who know how to avenge and stand up for themselves?
options: When gripped by a feeling of revenge, nothing else remains in their being but that feeling
They are calm and never feel the need for revenge
They always forgive their enemies instead
They think carefully before acting on revenge
reading.correct: When gripped by a feeling of revenge, nothing else remains in their being but that feeling
reading.explain: The passage says that once such people are gripped by the feeling of revenge, nothing else remains in their whole being but that feeling.

reading.ru: Кстати, перед стеной такие господа, то есть непосредственные люди и деятеля, искренне пасуют. Для них стена не отвод, как, например, для нас, людей, думающих, а, соответственно, ничего не делающих, не предлог воротиться с дороги, предлог, в который наш брат обыкновенно и сам не верит, но которому всегда очень рад.
reading.question: How do "immediate" (direct, unreflective) people behave in front of a wall, according to the narrator?
options: They sincerely give up, unlike thinking people who use the wall as an excuse to turn back
They always break through the wall by force
They ignore the wall completely
They build a new wall around it
reading.correct: They sincerely give up, unlike thinking people who use the wall as an excuse to turn back
reading.explain: The narrator contrasts immediate people, who sincerely pause before a wall, with thinking people like himself, for whom the wall is merely a pretext to turn back that they don't even believe in.

reading.ru: Ну, с такого-то вот непосредственного человека я считаю настоящим нормальным человеком, каким хотела его видеть сама нежная мать природа, любезно зарождая его на земле.
reading.question: What kind of man does the narrator say he considers the truly normal man, envying him bitterly?
options: The immediate (direct, unreflective) man, as nature intended him to be
The overly educated scholar
The wealthy nobleman
The professional soldier
reading.correct: The immediate (direct, unreflective) man, as nature intended him to be
reading.explain: He says he considers such an immediate man the truly normal man, exactly as tender mother nature wished to see him.

reading.ru: Я такому человеку до крайней желчи завидую. Он глуп.
reading.question: What does the narrator admit about the immediate man and his own feelings toward him?
options: He envies him to the point of bile, and admits the man is stupid
He despises him completely
He wants to become exactly like him but fails
He considers him a dangerous enemy
reading.correct: He envies him to the point of bile, and admits the man is stupid
reading.explain: The narrator says he envies such a man to the point of extreme bile, and admits plainly, "He is stupid."

reading.ru: Пусть это и усиленно сознающая мышь, но все-таки мышь, а тут человек, а следственно и прочее. И главное, он сам, сам ведь считает себя за мышь.
reading.question: How does the narrator characterize himself in contrast to the "immediate" man?
options: As a mouse of heightened consciousness, who nonetheless considers himself a mouse
As a lion who fears nothing
As equal in every way to the immediate man
As someone who has never doubted himself
reading.correct: As a mouse of heightened consciousness, who nonetheless considers himself a mouse
reading.explain: He says that even though it is a mouse of heightened consciousness, it is still a mouse, and importantly, it considers itself a mouse.

reading.ru: Положим, например, она тоже обижена. Она почти всегда бывает обижена и тоже желает отомстить.
reading.question: What is said about the "mouse" when it is offended?
options: It is almost always offended and also wishes to take revenge
It never feels offended at all
It immediately forgives the offender
It seeks help from others to take revenge
reading.correct: It is almost always offended and also wishes to take revenge
reading.explain: The text says the mouse is almost always offended and also wants to take revenge, just like the direct man.

reading.ru: Несчастная мышь, кроме одной первоначальной гадости, успела уже наградить кругом себя в виде вопросов и сомнений. Столько других гадостей к одному вопросу подвела столько неразрешенных вопросов, что по неволе кругом нее набирается какая-то роковая бурда, какая-то вонючая грязь, состоящая из ее сомнений, волнений.
reading.question: What does the unhappy "mouse" accumulate around itself, beyond its original nasty deed?
options: A mass of unresolved questions and doubts
A circle of loyal friends
Wealth and possessions
Fame and admiration
reading.correct: A mass of unresolved questions and doubts
reading.explain: The unhappy mouse manages to pile up around itself a mass of questions and unresolved doubts stemming from that one original nastiness.

reading.ru: Там, в своем мерзком, вонючем подполье, наша обиженная, прибитая и осмеянная мышь медленно погружается в холодную, ядовитую и, главное, вековечную злость.
reading.question: Where does the offended, beaten, and mocked "mouse" slowly sink into cold, poisonous, everlasting malice?
options: In its own foul, stinking underground
In a public square
In a church
In a royal court
reading.correct: In its own foul, stinking underground
reading.explain: The text says the mouse retreats to its foul, stinking underground, where it slowly sinks into cold, poisonous, everlasting malice.

reading.ru: Сорок лет сряду будет припоминать до последних самых постыдных подробностей свою обиду и при этом каждый раз прибавлять от себя подробности еще постыднейшие, злобно поддразнивая, раздражая себя собственной фантазией.
reading.question: What will the mouse do for forty years straight regarding its old insult?
options: Recall it down to the most shameful details, each time adding even more shameful ones
Forget it completely within a year
Tell everyone about it publicly
Write it down in a diary for others to read
reading.correct: Recall it down to the most shameful details, each time adding even more shameful ones
reading.explain: The text says that for forty years straight, the mouse will keep recalling its insult down to the last shameful detail, each time adding even more shameful ones from its own imagination.

reading.ru: На смерть Мадрея, опять-таки, все припомнят с накопившимися за все время процентами, но именно в этом холодном, омерзительном полуотчаянии, полуверии в этом конкуренте. В сознательном погребении самого себя заживо с горя, в подполе на 40 лет, в этой усиленно созданной и все-таки отчасти сомнительной безвыходности своего положения, во всем этом яде неудовлетворенных желаний, вошедших внутрь, Все эти лихорадки, колебания, принятых на веки решений и через минуты опять наступающих раскаяний, и заключается сок того странного наслаждения, о котором я говорил.
reading.question: How does the narrator describe the underground existence he imagines lasting forty years?
options: As the conscious burial of oneself alive, out of grief, in the underground
As a joyful retreat into nature
As a temporary escape before returning to society
As a punishment imposed by others
reading.correct: As the conscious burial of oneself alive, out of grief, in the underground
reading.explain: The passage describes the conscious burial of oneself alive out of grief, in the underground, for forty years.

reading.ru: Некоторые никогда не получали пощечин, и таким образом между вами намекнете мне, что я в мою жизнь, может быть, тоже испытал пощечину, потому и говорю, как знаток, без обзаклад, что вы это думаете. Ну, успокойтесь, господа, я не получал пощечин, хотя мне совершенно все равно, как вы думаете.
reading.question: What does the narrator say about slaps in the face, addressing his imagined audience?
options: Some people never received a slap, and the narrator himself has never received one either
Everyone in his life has received many slaps
He has given many slaps to others
Slaps are the only form of communication he understands
reading.correct: Some people never received a slap, and the narrator himself has never received one either
reading.explain: He notes some people have never received a slap in the face, and confesses he himself has never received one either, though he claims not to care what his listeners think.

reading.ru: Какая каменная стена?» Ну, разумеется, законы природы, выводы естественных наук, математика.
reading.question: What does the narrator say a "stone wall" actually consists of?
options: The laws of nature, the conclusions of natural science, and mathematics
A literal wall of brick and stone
The rules of etiquette in society
Religious commandments
reading.correct: The laws of nature, the conclusions of natural science, and mathematics
reading.explain: He explains that a "stone wall" simply means the laws of nature, the conclusions of the natural sciences, and mathematics.

reading.ru: Это дважды 24. Природа вас не спрашивается. Ей дело не до ваших желаний и до того, нравится ли вам ее закон или не нравится. Вы обязаны принимать ее так, как она есть, а следовательно и все ее результаты. Стена, значит, и есть стена.
reading.question: What attitude toward nature's laws does the narrator sarcastically describe here, using "twice two is four" and the idea that "a wall is a wall"?
options: That nature does not ask your permission and you must simply accept it and all its results
That nature can be persuaded to change through argument
That mathematics has no real authority over human life
That walls can always be torn down with enough effort
reading.correct: That nature does not ask your permission and you must simply accept it and all its results
reading.explain: The passage insists that nature does not ask whether you like its laws; you are obligated to accept it as it is, and, consequently, a wall simply is a wall.

reading.ru: Господи Боже, да какое мне дело до законов природы и арифметики, когда мне почему-нибудь эти законы и 2ЖД2А4 не нравятся. Разумеется, я не пробью такой стены лбом, если и в самом деле сил не будет пробить.
reading.question: What does the narrator say about the laws of nature and arithmetic that he personally dislikes?
options: He cares nothing for them, though he admits he cannot break such a wall by force if he lacks the strength
He has found a scientific way to disprove them
He has never encountered any laws he dislikes
He believes arithmetic does not apply to him
reading.correct: He cares nothing for them, though he admits he cannot break such a wall by force if he lacks the strength
reading.explain: He exclaims that he cares nothing for the laws of nature and arithmetic when he dislikes them, though he admits he won't break such a wall with his forehead if he truly lacks the strength.

reading.ru: Ха-ха-ха, да вы после этого и в зубной-то боли отыщите наслаждение, вскрикните вы со смехом. А что ж, и в зубной боли есть наслаждение, отвечу я.
reading.question: What does the narrator claim you will find even in a toothache?
options: Pleasure
Nothing but pain
A cure for boredom
A lesson in patience
reading.correct: Pleasure
reading.explain: He answers that yes, there is pleasure even in a toothache.

reading.ru: У меня целый месяц болели зубы, я знаю, что есть.
reading.question: How does the narrator claim to know that there is pleasure even in a toothache?
options: His teeth ached for a whole month, so he knows firsthand
He read about it in a medical journal
A doctor told him so
He imagined it without any experience
reading.correct: His teeth ached for a whole month, so he knows firsthand
reading.explain: He states that his teeth ached for a whole month, so he knows that there is indeed pleasure in it.

reading.ru: В этих-то стонах выражается наслаждение страдающего. Не ощущал бы он в них наслаждение, он бы и стонать не стал.
reading.question: What do the sufferer's groans express, according to the narrator?
options: The pleasure of the one suffering
Pure physical pain with no other meaning
A request for medical help
Anger at the doctor
reading.correct: The pleasure of the one suffering
reading.explain: He argues that these groans express the pleasure of the sufferer — if he felt no pleasure in them, he would not groan at all.

reading.ru: Вполне в рабстве ваших зубов, что захочет кто-то и перестанут болеть ваши зубы, а не захочет так и еще три месяца проболят.
reading.question: What realization about his own teeth does the sufferer's consciousness express, in the narrator's account?
options: That he is fully enslaved to his teeth, which will stop hurting only if someone else wills it
That he can cure the pain himself at any moment
That the pain will disappear if he ignores it
That his teeth are perfectly healthy
reading.correct: That he is fully enslaved to his teeth, which will stop hurting only if someone else wills it
reading.explain: The passage says the sufferer's consciousness expresses that he is entirely enslaved to his own teeth, which will stop aching only if someone else wishes it so.

reading.ru: Стоны его становятся какие-то скверные, пакостно злые и продолжаются по целым дням и ночам.
reading.question: How do the sufferer's groans change over several days of a toothache, according to the narrator?
options: They become nasty and spitefully malicious, continuing for days and nights
They stop entirely after the first day
They become quieter and more polite
They turn into laughter
reading.correct: They become nasty and spitefully malicious, continuing for days and nights
reading.explain: The narrator says the sufferer's groans become something nasty, spitefully malicious, and continue for whole days and nights.

reading.ru: Ну так вот, в этих-то всех сознаниях и позорах заключается сладострастие. Дескать, я вас беспокою, сердце вам надрываю, всем в доме спать не даю.
reading.question: What does the narrator say all this awareness and disgrace ultimately contains?
options: Voluptuous pleasure, in bothering others and keeping the household from sleep
Complete emptiness and meaninglessness
A cry for genuine sympathy
A plan to seek medical treatment
reading.correct: Voluptuous pleasure, in bothering others and keeping the household from sleep
reading.explain: He concludes that in all this awareness and disgrace lies voluptuous pleasure — he is bothering them, tearing at their hearts, not letting the household sleep.

reading.ru: Я для вас уж теперь не герой, каким прежде хотел казаться, а просто газенький человек Шенопан.
reading.question: How does the sufferer describe himself to his listeners, no longer wishing to seem a hero?
options: As a nasty little man
As a wise philosopher
As a brave warrior
As an innocent victim
reading.correct: As a nasty little man
reading.explain: He says he is no longer a hero to them, as he once wanted to seem, but simply a nasty little man.

reading.ru: Я очень рад, что вы меня раскусили. Вам скверно слушать мои подлинненькие стоны.
reading.question: How does the narrator react to the idea that his listeners have "seen through" him?
options: He is very glad they have seen through him, though it is unpleasant for them to hear his groans
He is furious and denies everything
He immediately stops speaking
He demands an apology from them
reading.correct: He is very glad they have seen through him, though it is unpleasant for them to hear his groans
reading.explain: He says he is very glad they have seen through him, admitting it is unpleasant for them to listen to his petty little groans.

reading.ru: Но ведь это от того, что я сам себя не уважаю. Разве сознающий человек может сколь-нибудь себя уважать?
reading.question: What reason does the narrator give for his awkward, distrustful jokes at the end of the chapter?
options: Because he does not respect himself
Because he is naturally cheerful
Because he wants to entertain his audience
Because he has had too much to drink
reading.correct: Because he does not respect himself
reading.explain: He explains that his jokes are awkward because he does not respect himself, asking whether a man of heightened consciousness could ever respect himself at all.
